title: An econ augment as the whole game plan

video.title: I took this broken new Econ Augment to try going Fast 9. It worked.

player.name: shurkou
player.about: Challenger climb content built around one idea per game. Useful for seeing how a single strong pick reshapes the plan for the next thirty minutes.

summary: A launch-week game where an econ augment is taken specifically to go fast 9, and the plan works. A long, unedited-feeling game that shows the whole econ arc from the pick to the level-9 board.
thesis: An econ augment is a loan against your HP: it pays gold now or per round and asks you to survive long enough to spend it. The pick is right when the HP plan exists (a board that holds stage 3 and 4 without rolling) and wrong when it does not. This game is the positive case; watch the HP as much as the gold, because that is what the augment is actually costing.

timeline.title: The econ pick and the HP it will cost
timeline.watch: The augment taken and the two alternatives. Write down his HP at 2-1 and check it again at 3-5 and 4-5: that difference is the price of the augment.
timeline.why: Econ augments are only correct with the health to cash them; below 50 HP at 4-1 the gold is worth less than the fights it did not win.
timeline.question: How much HP is he willing to spend to reach level 9? Where would you have pulled the plug?

timeline.title: Strongest board with the gold you are not spending
timeline.watch: How he keeps fights close in stage 2 without rolling: 2-stars fielded from natural shops, components combined early, cheap Wisps only when they save a streak.
timeline.why: A fast-9 player still needs to not lose every round; the free strength (upgrades from natural shops, early slams) is what makes the econ line survivable.

timeline.title: Interest, streak gold and the augment together
timeline.watch: Gold per round in stage 3: base income, interest, streak gold and the augment's payout. Add them up once; it explains why he can afford the levels later.
timeline.why: Income compounds from several sources at once; understanding the sum is what lets you decide how deep a rolldown can go two stages later.
timeline.question: What is his income at 3-5 including the augment? How many rounds until level 9 is paid for?

timeline.title: Levels on schedule, no roll before 8
timeline.watch: Level 6 at 3-2, 7 at 4-1, 8 at 4-2 or 4-5, and whether the shop is refreshed at all before 8. Note the HP each time.
timeline.why: The econ augment is wasted by a stage-3 roll: every gold rolled before 8 buys units at odds a third as good as the ones at 8.

timeline.title: The board that holds stage 4
timeline.watch: What keeps him alive through stage 4 while under-rolled: itemised frontline, a 2-star carry from natural copies, and positioning against the boards that could kill him.
timeline.why: Fast 9 is not 'do nothing until 9'; it is buying the minimum board that loses slowly while the gold accumulates.

timeline.title: Level 9 and the rolldown that follows
timeline.watch: The round he hits 9, how much gold is left, and the roll: which 5-costs he takes, in what order items move, and when he stops.
timeline.why: At 9 the 5-cost odds are five times what they were at 8; this is the roll the whole game was for, and it still needs a stop condition.
timeline.question: Before the roll: which two 5-costs fit his items? Would you take a third at the cost of two-starring a 4-cost?

timeline.title: Converting the cap into placements
timeline.watch: Players left and their HP; whether the capped board is positioned differently against each, and whether he keeps rolling or holds once the top 2 is locked.
timeline.why: A capped board still loses to bad positioning; the last stage is about the placement on the table, not more strength.

questions.q: When is an econ augment the wrong pick even if it is strong?
questions.a: When the board cannot hold stage 3 and 4 without rolling, or when HP is already low: the gold is only worth what it buys before you are eliminated, and below 50 HP at 4-1 that is not much.
HP in stages 3 and 4 and a weaker 4-2 board than the lobby's. It is paid back at 5-1 by 5-cost odds five times higher and a ninth slot, if you arrive with the gold and the health.

Because 4-cost odds at 6 are 5%, at 7 about 10% and at 8 about 30%; gold rolled at 6 or 7 buys the same units at a third of the rate. The augment makes the gold available; the discipline makes it worth something.

sourceNote: Title, channel, date and length come from the video page; the description says the game is a fast-9 attempt built around an econ augment. The stage guide is TFT Lab's reading of an econ-augment fast-9 game; the video has no creator chapters, so stops are anchored to stages.
